info.title: Klag HTTP API
info.summary: The HTTP surface of a self-hosted Klag instance.
info.description:
Klag is an open-source Kafka consumer lag exporter. It is self-hosted: you run the container (or native binary) next to your Kafka cluster, and it serves this API on `HTTP_PORT` (default 8888). There is no hosted Klag service and no API key — reachability and authorization are whatever your network and `MCP_AUTH_TOKEN` provide.

For questions *about* Klag rather than about your cluster, klag.dev hosts a read-only documentation MCP server at https://klag.dev/mcp.

servers.description: A self-hosted Klag instance. Replace host and port with your own deployment.

tags.name: mcp
tags.description: Read-only Model Context Protocol endpoint for AI agents.

get.description: Always returns 200 while the HTTP server is up. Does not check Kafka — use `/readyz` for that.

Returns 200 when any configured Kafka cluster is up, 503 when every cluster is down. One unreachable cluster does not fail readiness. The JSON body keeps a top-level `kafka` field (`connected` when any cluster is up) and a `clusters` array with per-cluster `kafka` status and `name` when the cluster is named. Each cluster's check runs every `KAFKA_HEALTH_CHECK_INTERVAL_MS` (default 30000).

200.description: At least one configured Kafka cluster is reachable.

503.description: Every configured Kafka cluster is unreachable; the instance is not ready to serve metrics.

get.description: Exposition-format metrics. Registered only when `METRICS_REPORTER=prometheus`; with any other reporter this path returns 404 and metrics are pushed to Datadog or the OTLP endpoint instead.

text/plain.example:
# HELP klag_consumer_lag Consumer lag per partition
# TYPE klag_consumer_lag gauge
klag_consumer_lag{consumer_group="orders",topic="events",partition="0"} 42.0

404.description: The Prometheus reporter is not enabled.

post.description:
Read-only Model Context Protocol endpoint over Streamable HTTP. Registered when `MCP_ENABLED=true`. Served from the metrics collector's in-memory snapshot — it never queries Kafka directly, so the tools report that the snapshot is not ready until metrics collection runs (`METRICS_REPORTER`). Path is configurable with `MCP_PATH`.

Methods: `initialize`, `ping`, `notifications/initialized`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`. Tools: `list_consumer_groups`, `get_consumer_group_lag`, `find_lagging_groups`, `diagnose`.

initializedNotification.summary: A notification (no id) — answered with 202 and no body

findLaggingGroups.summary: Find consumer groups above a lag threshold

200.description: A JSON-RPC 2.0 response. Tool-level failures are returned here as a result with `isError: true`, not as a JSON-RPC error.

202.description: The message was a JSON-RPC notification — any request without an `id`, such as `notifications/initialized`. Accepted with no response body, per JSON-RPC 2.0.

401.description: `MCP_AUTH_TOKEN` is set and the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header is missing or wrong. Rejected before JSON-RPC framing, so the body is a plain error object rather than a JSON-RPC envelope.

get.description: The endpoint is JSON-RPC over POST. GET returns 405 with an `Allow: POST` header; there is no SSE stream to open.

example.error: Method Not Allowed; use POST for JSON-RPC

mcpBearerToken.description: The value of `MCP_AUTH_TOKEN` on the Klag instance. When that variable is empty the endpoint is unauthenticated and Klag logs a warning at startup.

HealthResponse.description: Health check result. `kafka` and `clusters` are present on readiness responses only. Top-level `kafka` is connected when any cluster is connected.

kafka.description: Connected when any configured cluster is up.

clusters.description: Per-cluster Kafka status. `name` is omitted when the cluster is unnamed.

name.description: Configured cluster name (`cluster_name`); omitted when unnamed.

vertxVersion.description: Vert.x version Klag was built against.

javaVersion.description: Java runtime version, or the GraalVM native image's build JDK.

id.description: Request id, echoed back. Omit for notifications, which get no response body.

JsonRpcError.description: JSON-RPC 2.0 error envelope. Codes follow the specification: -32700 parse error, -32600 invalid request, -32601 method not found, -32602 invalid params, -32603 internal error.
